briefs.headline: India joins US-led group on structural excess capacity
briefs.deck: India has officially joined a coalition with the US and several other economies to tackle excess capacity. This coalition focuses on five sectors, including automobiles and semiconductors, that are primarily dominated by China. Countries in this group aim to coordinate actions against non-market practices that disrupt global markets. They plan to meet at a technical level before December 2026 to…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India has joined US and a dozen other economies, including Canada, EU, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, France, Germany and UK, on structural excess capacity in five categories - autos and EVs, batteries, chemicals, foundational semiconductors and solar panels - which are globally dominated by China.
The coalition will coordinate sectoral action and comes days after a meeting of trade ministers from G20 countries with the US taking a lead on the subject during its presidency of the grouping. Separately, the US trade representative is probing several countries, including India, for structural excess capacity under Section 301. The development is also significant as it comes weeks after US President Donald Trump met his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.
"We are concerned that, absent timely and effective actions, structural excess capacity and production in these sectors will cripple our domestic industries, displace local production, destroy jobs, undermine our economies, hinder efforts to develop and industrialise, and ultimately lower the standard of living for our people," a joint statement said.
The countries have sought an end to the use of non-market policies and practices that distort markets and contribute to the problem. 
China has for long been blamed by countries across the world for offering subsidies and dumping goods. The statement also noted that countries are taking individual action and the new group will work together "in new, dedicated sectoral platforms to further examine and take effective actions that address structural excess capacity and production in key sectors of concern".
"We are committed to meeting before Dec 2026, at the technical level, to develop terms of reference; share non-confidential information and data on structural excess capacity and production, its impact on these sectors, and efforts to mitigate the damage; and identify information gaps, drawing upon work of the OECD and other sources as appropriate. We commit to exploring effective and, whenever possible, complementary actions to defend our economies from the negative impact on trade and workers created by structural excess capacity and production. Working together, we aim to create the conditions necessary so that market-oriented competition in affected sectors can thrive once again," the statement said.
In 2016, in Shanghai, G20 trade ministers released a statement expressing concern about excess capacity in certain industries and its negative impacts on trade and workers, and a few months later, it was also endorsed by leaders from these countries at Hangzhou.

briefs.headline: MDR on UPI may now take effect in January 2027
briefs.deck: The rollout of the merchant discount rate on UPI transactions has been postponed to January 2027. This decision follows requests from trade bodies concerned about potential impacts on festival season sales. The new fee structure was originally set to take effect on October 15, giving stakeholders only a month for preparations. The framework includes a 0.4% charge for transactions above Rs 2,000…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The rollout of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions is expected to be postponed to Jan 2027 against the earlier date of Oct 15 with an announcement expected over the next couple of days.
The move follows representations from trade bodies which were apprehensive that the introduction of the fees may impact festival season sales at a time when prices are rising. They have argued that introducing the fee during the festival season, when retail activity and digital payments typically rise, could increase costs for merchants and weigh on sales.
A postponement will also give businesses more time to prepare for the implementation of MDR, which has been pushed by banks and RBI.
The MDR framework was approved and notified by NPCI on Sept 15, with a 0.4% charge for eligible person-to-merchant (M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. The framework was to take effect from Oct 15, giving banks, payment aggregators and other ecosystem participants a month to make operational changes.
The framework was designed to create a revenue stream for the payments ecosystem after more than six years of effectively zero MDR on UPI. Govt had said the levy would apply only to specified merchant transactions, with payments up to Rs 2,000 and eligible small merchants continuing to remain free. About 96% of M transactions were expected to remain unaffected.

briefs.headline: Faceless system in place for central GST payers
briefs.deck: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman unveiled a faceless GST system to streamline processes for two lakh taxpayers. This new system follows significant rate cuts that reduced the effective GST rate across goods and services. A working group submitted a report to implement a centralized tax administration for multiple CGST jurisdictions. This initiative aims to improve taxpayer experiences similar…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Thursday announced a faceless system for 2 lakh central GST payers operating in multiple states, following up on rate rationalisation and process reforms undertaken by the Centre and the states.
After last year's rate cuts, the effective GST rate on all goods and services has come down from 11.8% to 10.8%. Together with the procedural simplification, 99% of the issues have been resolved, FM said, adding that rate changes will now be an annual feature that will be implemented from April every year.
"For the next-gen GST reforms, 99% of the issues have been addressed. Everything on the process and rate side has been driven from a principle of trust," she said, adding that govt was keeping the door open for further fine-tuning, as and when required.
"Going forward, we intend to bring a centralised tax administration for these multiple CGST jurisdiction for taxpayers with a unified window for all their CGST-related functions of scrutiny of returns, audit, adjudication, appeal, taxpayer services and grievance redressal," she told reporters, while asserting the Centre's initiative.
A working group within the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has submitted its report, and the proposed framework would be put up for public consultation before the next budget and will be implemented during the next financial year.
The FM said the faceless approach adopted in income tax was appreciated by taxpayers and the Centre intended to bring in the same reform in the administration of GST.
Sitharaman clarified that it was a govt initiative and had nothing to do with the GST Council. She said there were nearly 69.5 lakh taxpayers registered under the CGST administration, which included these two lakh taxpayers under multiple GST jurisdictions.
Administrative control over GST taxpayers has been divided between the central and state tax authorities based on a specific turnover-based formula determined by the GST Council to ensure a single interface. While administrative control over 90% of taxpayers, who have turnover below Rs 1.5 crore, has been kept under state tax administration, the remaining 10% is with the central administration.
Taxpayers with turnover above Rs 1.5 crore are divided equally between the central and state tax administrations.

MUMBAI: With Brent crude prices spiking again to over $105 per barrel, US Treasury bond yields rising to a more than two-decade high and the rupee at close to 96.8/$, strong foreign fund selling pulled the markets sharply down on Thursday.

The day's slide wiped out Rs 10 lakh crore worth of investors' wealth with the aggregate market capitalisation of companies listed on BSE at Rs 461 lakh crore, official data showed.
Post Thursday's close, sensex was the worst-performing index this year among most of the major benchmarks around the world. Compared to a 16% year-to-date drop in sensex, Nifty is down 15%, Hang Seng in Hong Kong is down nearly 10% while Shanghai Composite for mainland China is down 5.3%.
At the other end of the spectrum is Japan's Nikkei that's up 33% while Brazil's iBovespa is up 28% and technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite, boosted by the strong rally in AI stocks, is up 17.6%.
Till Oct 1, sensex had an eight-week losing streak, the longest in 25 years, which started in the week ended Aug 7 when the index had closed at 78,499 points. 
From that level, the index is now down a little over 6,900 points or 8.8%. In case sensex closes below its Oct 1 level of 71,910 points, the nine-week losing streak would be its longest on record.
Since its Aug 7 close, thanks to the continuous selling, investors' wealth loss stands at Rs 32.3 lakh crore. This is despite the addition of several companies to the list of stocks traded on BSE after their IPO which includes NSE, currently having a market capitalisation of Rs 4.3 lakh crore. briefs.headline: GST Council scraps tax officers' arrest powers, eases refund rules
briefs.deck: The GST Council has proposed major procedural changes to enhance business operations and tax compliance. These reforms aim to streamline registration, refunds, and input tax credit processes while lowering compliance costs. Additionally, the council will remove officers' powers for arrests under the GST framework. Processing of refunds will be expedited, with a goal to resolve claims within three…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Nine years after the biggest indirect reform in the country, GST Council on Friday decided on a massive procedural overhaul that will rework the way businesses operate, enable them to get refunds and credit for taxes paid, allow for movement of trucks with fewer stoppages and do away with officers' arrest powers.
From registration and returns to refunds decriminalisation the second part of GST2.0 was completed with the elements to be rolled out from April, allowing for amendments to the law and for the systems to be revamped.
Amid the unanimity at the all-powerful body led by finance minister 
Nirmala Sitharaman
, there were two subjects on which decisions were deferred.
First, the proposal to only stop input tax credit (ITC) for entities that have collected tax, but not deposited it, while allowing it for others in the chain to claim credit was referred to a panel of officers.
The committee has been tasked with finalising its recommendations and coming back to the Council within three months so that it can be ready by April, Sitharaman told reporters after the six-hour meeting.
Focus on faster decisions, lower compliance costs: PM
PM Narendra Modi, in a social media post, said, “The Council’s recommendations on removal of arrest provisions, greater decriminalisation and simpler procedures will have a very positive impact. The focus is clear: Faster decisions. 
Lower compliance costs. Automated refunds. Trust-based administration. These are in line with our constant efforts to make GST more efficient, transparent and citizen-friendly.”
After the meeting, Sitharaman said states and the Centre have worked together to move to a trust-based regime for taxpayers.
One of the most significant changes is to do away with arrest powers for officers under section 69 of Central GST (CGST) Act. While the powers were not available under the VAT regime, the threat of arrest has often been dangled by officials. Separately, the monetary threshold for prosecution has also been raised five-fold to Rs 5 crore, while also rationalising punishment under section 132 of CGST Act.
Even dispute resolution has been reformed with the Council deciding against issuing notices in cases where the tax involved is under Rs 10,000. What’s more, even in the ongoing 12 lakh-odd cases, notices will be withdrawn.
Further, while penalties will be deemed to be a “charge”, where tax is paid voluntarily, in non-fraud cases a reduced penalty of 5% will be imposed if the interest is paid within 30 days or 60 days in case of adjudication. The maximum general penalty is also sought to be slashed from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000 and the upper-limit for pre-deposit in case of filing of appeals will be capped at Rs 40 crore.
In a bid to reduce truck stoppages, officials in states other than the origin and destination will no longer be able to intercept vehicles. And, even in cases where it is allowed by an officer of the rank of a joint commissioner, it can only be done when there is specific information, FM told reporters, while asserting that the decisions have been taken to ensure that life becomes easier for businesses and is part of the “reforms express”.
The other major change is on the refunds front, where the idea is to process 90% of the claims within three days and reduce the period of acknowledgement from 15 days to 10, with a system of deemed acknowledgement introduced.
A host of input tax credit related simplifications have been introduced allowing businesses to claim refunds of the accumulated input tax credit related to capital goods. Starting Nov, the facility can be spread over 60 months and will come as a boost to long-gestation projects. Similarly, restrictions on ITC use have been removed for supplies such as health and life insurance, outdoor catering, free samples, telecom towers and pipelines laid in factories.
Host of simplifications
A host of simplifications have also been offered for the services sector, which will benefit exports. From small businesses with up to Rs 5 crore turnover and selling only to consumers (B2C), GST Council approved in-principle a plan to allow filing of annual returns.
Besides, those selling on e-commerce platforms will not be required to register in multiple states, helping 90% of such sellers.
There was a host of registration related rationalisation, meant to ensure that most businesses can register in three days, while allowing changes automatically, apart from altering the principal place of business. Even returns were sought to be simplified to automate details and work towards an invoice management system.

briefs.headline: Cochin Shipyard gets order to build 40 ships from U.S., Germany, Norway, other nations: Sonowal
briefs.deck: A senior Shipping Ministry official said that some Russian entities have also shown interest in building ships in India
briefs.bodyText:
State-owned Cochin Shipyard has received orders to build over 40 ships from the U.S., Germany, Norway and other countries, Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said on Thursday.
Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Mr. Sonowal said the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways is creating a comfortable ecosystem for shipbuilding.
"Most of the orders we are receiving for shipbuilding are for Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) from foreign countries like Germany, America, and Norway. So far, we have received orders for more than 40 ships," he said.
A senior Shipping Ministry official said that some Russian entities have also shown interest in building ships in India, in collaboration with Indian shipyards, including Cochin Shipyard.
The Minister said Indian shipbuilders are earning credibility globally.
"That is the reason why we are getting this number of orders, and this reflects how India could generate confidence about its quality production, about its capacity building," he added.
Responding to a question, Mr. Sonowal said during the second day of the 3rd 'Sagarmanthan - The Ocean Dialogue', he met a Myanmar minister, who informed him that coastal shipping in Myanmar is successfully running.
"So, that is why this Sittwe Port in Myanmar is very successfully operating," he said.
The Minister also said he held bilateral talks with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan to advance port investment, green shipping and regional connectivity, and Belgium has expressed its willingness to work with India to promote shipbuilding.
An official statement said that a delegation from the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani) and Sonowal discussed its participation in Indian port projects such as Vadhavan and Galathea Bay.
"The two sides also discussed cooperation in shipbuilding, seafarer training and resilient supply chains.”
"Saudi Arabia expressed their interest in investing in India’s port projects and in the Maritime Development Fund (MDF)," it said.
The statement also said that during the second day of the 3rd 'Sagarmanthan - The Ocean Dialogue', VOC Port has signed an agreement with the Port of Antwerp Port for training in capacity building in green shipping and green fuel.
Over the last twelve years, India's port capacity has risen from 1,561 to 2,817 MTPA, cargo handled from 1,052 to 1,668 million tonnes and inland waterways cargo from 29 to 218 million tonnes, while median container vessel turnaround has fallen from 35 to 23 hours.

briefs.headline: US sanctions Indian firms, individuals as Iran oil crackdown widens
briefs.deck: On Thursday, the United States targeted two Mumbai-based companies over their alleged oil trade involvement with Iran. The sanctions affected five Indian nationals connected to SSPL Solutions Private Limited and Samudra Marine Services Private Limited. These measures are part of a broader crackdown on Iran under 'Operation Economic Outcast'. The U.S. government aims to curb Iranian oil revenues…
briefs.bodyText:
The United States on Thursday imposed sanctions on two Mumbai-based companies and five Indian nationals over their alleged involvement in the trade of petroleum products from Iran, as Washington stepped up its economic pressure on Tehran.
The US department of state targeted SSPL Solutions Private Limited and Samudra Marine Services Private Limited for allegedly facilitating the import of petroleum products from Iran.
The action also blocked five individuals associated with the two firms from carrying out transactions related to their respective companies, according to news agency PTI.
Two people linked to SSPL Solutions, Dhwani Vora and Nisarg Vora, were sanctioned, while Ketan Kochikar, Bhupendrasingh Sahu and Harishyam Hariharan Chundakattil, associated with Samudra Marine Services, were also targeted.
US expands sanctions over Iranian petroleum trade
The sanctions against the Indian entities and individuals are part of the US crackdown on Iran under “Operation Economic Outcast”.
“The department of state is sanctioning ten entities, six individuals, and five vessels in connection with trade in Iranian-origin petroleum, petroleum products, and petrochemical products,” the US state department said in an official statement.
The department alleged that the targeted entities channelled millions of dollars to the Iranian regime, strengthening what it described as one of Tehran’s most important revenue streams and enabling its continued illicit conduct.
“The US government is imposing sanctions on both the buyers and sellers driving this trade in Iranian petrochemical products,” the department said.
At the same time, the US authorised wind-down transactions involving Samudra Marine Services until October 23.
A wind-down period allows parties to complete existing transactions and exit operations before sanctions or liquidation measures fully take effect.
Treasury targets 17 entities and shadow fleet vessels
Separately, the US treasury department sanctioned 17 entities and their associated shadow fleet vessels as part of the same effort to restrict Iranian oil revenues.
“Treasury is starving the tyrannical regime in Tehran of the money it uses to wage war in the region, and we will continue exposing those who enable the regime’s oil sales,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
“No enabler of Iranian sanctions evasion is safe from the full force of Treasury's authorities,” he added.
A Treasury official told reporters that the measures represented what the department described as its “most significant blow yet to Iran’s remaining illicit maritime infrastructure”.
“Today's action represents the most significant blow yet to Iran's remaining illicit maritime infrastructure by neutralizing the vast majority of the shadow fleet,” the official said.
According to Reuters, the Treasury official said the operation was aimed at cutting Tehran’s funding for the war, missile construction, cyberattacks and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
Pressure on Iranian oil exports
The latest sanctions come after the US reimposed its blockade of Iranian ports on July 14 following the breakdown of a memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran.
A Treasury official said Iran had about 20 million barrels of crude oil remaining on vessels outside the blockade. The global oil market consumes about 100 million barrels per day.

stories.headline: 'Our cameras will be sharp': Broadcaster takes a dig at Australia
stories.deck: South African sports broadcaster SuperSport has taken a dig at Australia ahead of their first Test series in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate. Australia will face South Africa in a three-match series, with the opening Test scheduled at Kingsmead in Durban on Friday, October 9, at 1 pm IST.
stories.bodyText:
South African sports broadcaster SuperSport has taken a dig at Australia ahead of their first Test series in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate. Australia will face South Africa in a three-match series, with the opening Test scheduled at Kingsmead in Durban on Friday, October 9, at 1 pm IST.
SuperSport posted a promo on X ahead of the three-Test series, saying its cameras “will be sharp”. The post included a camera emoji, bringing back memories of the incident at Newlands in Cape Town in 2018.
SuperSport's cameras caught Bancroft in 2018
SuperSport's reference goes back to March 24, 2018, when its cameras caught Australian batter Cameron Bancroft working on the ball with a small yellow object during a Test against South Africa at Newlands.
The footage showed Bancroft using the object on the ball before putting it down his trousers. The incident led to the ball-tampering scandal that came to be known as Sandpapergate.
The footage was shown on the big screen at the ground. Australia's then head coach Darren Lehmann sent a message to 12th man Peter Handscomb, while the incident quickly became a major talking point in cricket.
SuperSport's cameras had also been asked to look out for anything unusual during the series after the umpires reportedly became suspicious about Australia's efforts to alter the ball.
The broadcaster's coverage included more than 30 cameras, with 18 operated by camera crews.
Several Australia players return with memories of 2018
Australia's current squad includes several players who were part of the team during the Newlands scandal.
Steve Smith, who was Australia's captain at the time, is now vice-captain under Pat Cummins. Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon also played at Newlands in 2018. Matthew Renshaw, who joined the squad as a replacement for the final Test of that series, is also back in the team. 
David Warner has retired, while Cameron Bancroft has not played a Test for more than six years.
The scandal has received more attention in the Australian media than in South Africa in recent weeks. However, the team could still face some reminders of the incident during the tour.
Australia return to Newlands for the third Test
South Africa enter the series as reigning World Test Championship winners after beating Australia in last year's final at Lord's. Australia, meanwhile, will look to collect points in the 2025-27 World Test Championship cycle. The second Test will be played in Gqeberha from October 18.
The third Test, scheduled to begin at Newlands on October 27, will bring Australia back to the venue where the 2018 scandal unfolded.

stories.headline: ‘You can’t beat experience’: India coach explains Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return
stories.deck: The selection framework for India's cricket team has notably included VVS Laxman, aimed at fostering better communication about player fitness and rehabilitation. Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return to the T20I squad underscores the strategy of leveraging experience for critical matches ahead. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak highlights the blend of seasoned players with fresh talent, ensuring that while the…
stories.bodyText:
Ranchi: Centre of Excellence head 
VVS Laxman
’s new role in India’s selection process and 
Bhuvneshwar Kumar
’s return to the T20I squad for the upcoming New Zealand tour point to the same priority: better communication and greater experience as India look to build beyond their current winning combination.
Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said 
Jasprit Bumrah
’s absence during parts of India’s recent schedule had highlighted the value of having an experienced bowler around the younger group.
“We all know you can’t beat experience. The youngsters are also performing well, but at some stage you need that experience,” Kotak said.
Conditions in New Zealand may suit the 36-year-old Bhuvneshwar.
“Bhuvneshwar has been doing really well in the IPL for the last two seasons. So the selectors must have thought that, for New Zealand conditions and all, we need some experience,” Kotak said.
Laxman’s inclusion in selection meetings is intended to ensure that information on players undergoing rehabilitation, particularly their fitness status, reaches the selectors directly.
“(Head coach) Gautam (Gambhir) always speaks to Laxman. That is the normal procedure, which I have always seen,” Kotak said.
Kotak said India’s winning run would not come at the cost of developing their bench strength.
“When you test your bench, if you win, the process continues. If you lose, there is a very thin line between maintaining that balance,” he said.

stories.deck: “Bhuvneshwar has been doing really well in the IPL for the last two seasons, so the selectors must have thought that he would be useful in New Zealand,” Kotak elaborated
stories.bodyText:
Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s inclusion in the T20I squad for the New Zealand series created enough buzz to spill into India’s press conference ahead of the second T20I against the West Indies — a good two weeks before the Men in Blue take on the Kiwis.
Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak is neither a selector nor a bowling expert, yet he obliged when asked about the reasons behind the 36-year-old’s recall.
“The obvious thing is it’s the selectors [who made the decision]. I can give you an answer on what I think. In England, I felt we needed experience along with the young bowlers as Jasprit Bumrah was also not available there. We all know that you can’t beat experience,” Kotak said at the JSCA Stadium on Thursday (October 8, 2026).
“Bhuvneshwar has been doing really well in the IPL for the last two seasons, so the selectors must have thought that he would be useful in New Zealand,” he elaborated.
When asked if Mohammed Shami had a similar chance, Kotak explained: “If the selectors feel that he is doing well and the team has a requirement, then any player can be selected.”
The BCCI’s decision to include Centre of Excellence head V.V.S. Laxman in selection meetings has been another raging topic.
“I believe the BCCI took that decision for a purpose. I have worked with Laxman for three years in the CoE. He used to tell us that if the Indian team has any requirement, then our first duty is to do it. We used to postpone our leaves if an important player [came to the CoE] and the Indian team wanted him immediately. That’s how committed Laxman is. So, whatever role he will be in, I am sure that Laxman will think about what is best for Indian cricket”.

stories.headline: India’s Para Asian Games contingent gets warm send-off, Mandaviya launches new jersey
stories.deck: Para-badminton star Pramod Bhagat was named the flag bearer of the Indian contingent for the Games
stories.bodyText:
India's Para Asian Games contingent received a formal send-off on Thursday ahead of the continental showpiece in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launching the new Team India jersey at a ceremony organised by the Paralympic Committee of India.
The ceremony began with the traditional lighting of the lamp and was attended by prominent para-athletes, including Paralympic medallists Simran Sharma, Preeti Pal and Kapil Parmar, besides para-archer Rakesh Kumar and para-powerlifter Ashok Kumar.
Para-badminton star Pramod Bhagat was named the flag bearer of the Indian contingent for the Games. PCI president Devendra Jhajharia, chairperson Payal Kanodia and head coach Satyanarayana were also present.
Mr. Mandaviya hailed the para-athletes for overcoming challenges and urged them to now focus on winning medals for the country.
"Para-athletes are those young people who have already won the battle of life. It is not a small thing to challenge nature and move ahead," Mr. Mandaviya said.
"You have already won the journey of life. But now, you also have to conquer the journey of medals."
Mr. Mandaviya said athletes were receiving the necessary support from the government, federations and the Indian Olympic Association.
"Today, our athletes, whether para-athletes or able-bodied athletes, have no shortage of support. From the government, from the federation, from the Olympic Association — whatever support is needed is available to them. The government stands firmly behind them," he said.
Drawing an analogy with the Mahabharata, Mr. Mandaviya urged the athletes to remain focused on their targets.
"We have to identify our target with passion, commitment and dedication. We have to be successful. We have to win," he said.
"And athletes never lose. Either they win or they learn."
Head coach Satyanarayana expressed confidence in India's medal prospects, particularly in para-athletics, while acknowledging the difficult selection process after the quota was reduced from 130 to 60.
"We will get medals till 95. In athletics, the number of athletes in the contingent is 60. Not even one will be less. Keep this in mind. That is why we have conducted the selection process very well," he said.
"The athletes are also very confident. All of them are fit. Para athletics is starting from the 19th, and from the 19th, we will start with the gold medal."
Satyanarayana said the reduced quota had left several athletes disappointed but maintained that those selected had made the team on merit.
"This time the quota has been reduced. It was 130 quota, and from 130 we have come down to 60. Seventy people have been cut. If someone had it in his mind that, 'I am fourth, I will be selected', but he was not selected, then there is bound to be disappointment," he said.
"We have also made a lot of effort. I have pain from inside, that is why I have pain. But whoever is making the team has real talent. He has the eligibility. I do not have that much quota. That is why we have had to leave some athletes out."
Discus thrower Suvarna Raj said an injury six months ago had briefly raised doubts about her participation but she now feels confident of winning a medal.
"They have made me so strong that this time I promise that I will get a medal," she said.
Suvarna also backed India to return with a three-figure medal tally despite the smaller contingent.
"The medal tally will remain in the triple digits, don't worry, and it will also increase in the triple digits. You see, last time we reached 120, this time we are going to 60, but still we are promising that we will come back in the triple digits," she said.
Bhagat, who was named flag bearer, said the honour was particularly special after a difficult period in his career.
"Definitely, there are ups and downs in life, and I have gone through a tough time. But finally, it is said that after sorrow comes happiness. My hurdles have been overcome, and finally, I have been made a flag bearer, which is a very big thing in itself," he said.
Bhagat also said that he would aim for gold at the Games.
"Definitely, all of you have the hope that when Pramod Bhagat goes, he will get gold. I will try not to disappoint you. My preparation is very good, and I will try to get gold for all of you," he said.

briefs.headline: BCCI Centre of Excellence treated 32 top cricketers last year
briefs.deck: The BCCI's Centre of Excellence reported a rise in rehabilitated players, with 32 men undergoing treatment recently. A budget increase of nearly Rs 35 crore was allocated for injury management and rehabilitation. Soft-tissue injuries predominated among the cases, with notable players affected. Communication issues between Team India and the CoE's Sports Science Medicine team have been highlighted.
briefs.bodyText:
New Delhi: The Indian cricket board’s (
BCCI
) injury management programme at its Centre of Excellence (CoE) has been under renewed focus over the past 20 months. Now, according to the CoE annual report, accessed by TOI, as many as 32 top men’s team players, including 20 BCCI centrally contracted players and 12 players under a new targeted/India ‘A’ category, underwent rehabilitation for injuries between April 2025 and March 2026. The list has swelled post IPL 2026, with at least two players breaking down in each series.
Interestingly, the report states that the BCCI increased the CoE’s budget by nearly Rs 35 crore compared to the actual expenses in the previous financial year. The CoE’s expenses include administrative costs, courses and match expenses.
The CoE’s projected expenses for 2026-27 now stand at Rs 127 crore, compared to Rs 92 crore in actual expenses last year.
India’s Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir have been vocal about how difficult it has become to plan tours because of a surge in injuries over the last year. While the report does not specify how many times each player reported to the CoE, it mentions that injuries to 68 players across genders were treated and managed by the BCCI-CoE Sports Science Medicine (SSM) team.
When it comes to the nature of the injuries, the majority were soft-tissue injuries. 
The only impact injury treatment mentioned was that of Rishabh Pant, who underwent treatment following a foot fracture sustained during a Test in Manchester in July 2025.
Interestingly, the report also reveals that Rohit Sharma underwent rehabilitation at the CoE during this period, but the BCCI never made an official statement about it. Rohit last reported to the CoE for a hamstring injury following this year’s IPL.
The latest Team India players added to the list up to Sept 30 this year are Virat Kohli, Varun Chakravarthy, Prince Yadav and Harsh Dubey, besides multiple ‘targeted’ players. From that list, Jasprit Bumrah, Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Harshit Rana, Hardik Pandya and Prasidh Krishna have been repeat cases. Rana, Pandya and Reddy have each spent at least four months at the CoE in the last 18 months.
No SSM head, lack of coordination with Team India
The BCCI advertised the post of SSM head at the CoE only last month. The post has been lying vacant since Nitin Patel resigned in March 2025.
TOI understands that there has been a breakdown in communication between Team India’s SSM team and the CoE’s SSM team, with cricket head 
VVS Laxman
 being the only medium of communication. It has been learnt that Team India strength and conditioning (S&C) coach Adrian Le Roux suggested a few tweaks to workload management routines in June 2025, while the CoE has been reluctant to deviate from its own mechanisms.
Personnel from the CoE’s SSM team travelled to domestic tournaments to monitor key India players under the injury prevention and management programme.
The last time Indian cricket saw a spate of soft-tissue injuries was in 2021-22, when players suddenly moved out of playing in bubbles during the Covid-19 pandemic. That time, the issue was brought under control in two to three months. In 2017, too, there was a three-month phase when multiple players broke down after S&C coach Shanker Basu introduced drastic changes to the fitness programme.
Fifteen budgeted camps didn’t happen
According to the report, 15 of the 57 budgeted camps and tournaments were not conducted in the last audited year.
The CoE conducted 25 elite/high-performance camps across age groups and genders, besides special camps for the north-eastern states. It also organised multiple courses and camps for S&C coaches, other coaches and match officials.
Thirty-seven top men’s players opted for ‘training block’ programme
The CoE started a programme called the ‘training block’ for contracted and targeted/India ‘A’ players. According to the report, 37 players, including 11 contracted players and 26 India ‘A’/targeted players, availed themselves of the programme, which focuses on strength and skill training.

briefs.headline: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's explosive net session raises big question: Will he play in Ranchi?
briefs.deck: The young batter went on an attacking spree in the nets, repeatedly hitting the ball over the boundary and towards the stands. With every big hit, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi showed why he has become one of the most talked-about young batters in the Indian squad.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may still be waiting for his chance to play for India, but the 15-year-old made sure everyone noticed him during the team's practice session ahead of the second T20I against the West Indies in Ranchi on Friday.
The young batter went on an attacking spree in the nets, repeatedly hitting the ball over the boundary and towards the stands. With every big hit, Sooryavanshi showed why he has become one of the most talked-about young batters in the Indian squad.
His aggressive batting also came at a time when India have a selection question to consider at the top of the order. 
Sanju Samson
 managed just 11 runs in the opening T20I, giving the young Bihar batter another opportunity to make his case for a place in the playing XI.
Sooryavanshi makes his presence felt
With policemen, spectators and media personnel gathering around the nets, Sooryavanshi attracted plenty of attention with his powerful hitting. The teenager sent several deliveries sailing towards the stands and the sight screen near the press conference hall.
While the senior players went through their practice routines, Sooryavanshi made the most of his time in the nets. His attacking approach offered a glimpse of the fearless batting that has brought him into the conversation around India's top-order options.
Samson's 11 runs open up the selection debate
Samson scored only 11 runs in the opening T20I, which India won by eight wickets. His performance has added interest to the question of whether India will make any changes to their batting combination for the second match.
Sooryavanshi's powerful hitting in the nets has given the selectors another option to consider.
India assistant coach Sitanshu Kotak said the team had not finalised its playing XI.
"The team has not been decided yet, so I don't know what the chances are. Everyone in the squad has a chance," Kotak said ahead of the second T20I in Ranchi.
India won the first T20I in Lucknow by eight wickets and will look to take a 2-0 lead in the five-match series in Ranchi.

briefs.headline: 'Tell your story': Pat Cummins' blunt response to Khawaja's book on Sandpapergate
briefs.deck: Australia captain Pat Cummins has played down concerns that Usman Khawaja’s upcoming autobiography could bring fresh attention to the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate. Australia are returning to South Africa for the first time since the scandal. The three-Test series begins at Kingsmead on Friday, but Cummins said the incident had already been dealt with and the team had…
briefs.bodyText:
Australia captain 
Pat Cummins
 has played down concerns that 
Usman Khawaja
’s upcoming autobiography could bring fresh attention to the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate.
Australia are returning to South Africa for the first time since the scandal. The three-Test series begins at Kingsmead on Friday, but Cummins said the incident had already been dealt with and the team had moved on.
Cummins says the team has moved on
Cummins was part of the Australian bowling attack during the Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. Australia were caught using sandpaper to rough up one side of the ball illegally to generate more swing.
The scandal created a major crisis for Cricket Australia. Captain Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught with sandpaper in his pocket, were banned for their roles in the incident.
Cummins and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon denied knowing about the ball-tampering.
All four are now back in South Africa for the three-Test series.
Cummins confirmed that he had spoken to Khawaja, who was also part of the Australian team during the 2018 Test at Newlands. However, he said they did not discuss the matter in detail.
“Didn't go back into too much detail. He just basically gave me the heads-up that he's doing a book, and yeah, as always, no worries. 
Tell your story. It's fine,” Cummins said.
Khawaja’s book could revisit the scandal
Australian media reports have said that Khawaja had wanted the entire team to accept collective responsibility after the scandal. However, the suggestion was reportedly rejected at the time.
Cummins said he did not know what Khawaja had written in his autobiography, which is due to be published next month.
“You need to ask him,” he said. “It’s obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times. So, yeah, it was dealt with then. Now all I can say is, as a group, we moved on, very happy with the last eight years, how we’ve been as a group and evolved.”
Broadcaster takes a dig at Australia
South African broadcaster SuperSport, whose cameras captured the ball-tampering incident in 2018, has also brought the episode back into focus.
The broadcaster shared a social media clip showing Bancroft using sandpaper on the ball and the Australian team’s reaction after the players were caught.
SuperSport added a warning ahead of the upcoming series, saying: “Our cameras will be sharp for this 3-match test series.”

briefs.headline: Abhishek Sharma on the cusp of breaking Suryakumar Yadav’s unique T20I record
briefs.deck: Abhishek Sharma is on the brink of achieving a remarkable milestone, needing just 53 runs to cross 2,000 T20I runs during the second T20I against West Indies. With a chance to eclipse Suryakumar Yadav's record for the fastest attainment of this feat, Sharma's current high strike rate demonstrates his game-changing prowess.
briefs.bodyText:
Abhishek Sharma
 could turn Friday's second T20I against the West Indies into another landmark night in his rapidly evolving international career. The India opener needs just 53 runs to complete 2,000 T20I runs, but the milestone itself is only half the story.
If Abhishek gets there quickly enough, he could take down a record currently held by none other than his former captain and one of the most explosive batters in T20 cricket, 
Suryakumar Yadav
.
SKY's 1,164-ball record in sight
Suryakumar holds the world record for reaching 2,000 T20I runs in the fewest balls. He reached the landmark in 1,164 deliveries, surpassing Australia's Aaron Finch, who had taken 1,283 balls.
Abhishek currently has 1,947 runs from 997 balls. That means he has 167 balls as a theoretical maximum to score the 53 runs and equal SKY's 1,164-ball mark.
But if he wants to break the record, he must get to 2,000 in 1,163 balls or fewer, meaning he has to score those 53 runs within his next 166 balls.
A record tailor-made for Abhishek's approach
Abhishek has built his reputation around an attacking brand of T20 cricket. His current T20I career strike rate stands at a staggering 195.29, with 1,947 runs coming from just 997 deliveries. He has also already smashed 135 sixes and three centuries in the format.
The left-hander has shown just how quickly he can change a game. 
Earlier this year, he smashed a T20I century in only 30 balls against Afghanistan, the fastest century by an Indian in the format.
So while 53 runs may sound like a modest target, the real question on Friday will be: how quickly can he get there?
West Indies stand in the way
Abhishek made a brisk start in the series opener in Lucknow, scoring 21 off 10 balls before Roston Chase dismissed him. India went on to win by eight wickets, with 
Shreyas Iyer
 smashing an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls to give the hosts a 1-0 lead.
Now, with Ranchi hosting the second T20I, Abhishek has the chance to turn a personal milestone into a piece of T20I history.

briefs.headline: Indians love Formula 1, would love to race there: Lando Norris
briefs.deck: The Indian government recently formed a task force to revive the marquee race which was dropped after three editions from 2011-2013 due to taxation and financial hurdles
briefs.bodyText:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris on Thursday (October 8, 2026) expressed a strong desire to race in India amid the country's push to bring Formula 1 back to its shores.
The Indian government recently formed a task force to revive the marquee race which was dropped after three editions from 2011-2013 due to taxation and financial hurdles.
The new owners of the Buddh Circuit in Greater Noida, Adani Group, have had talks with Formula One Management on the mega event but it is unlikely the race could be held in the near future.
Responding to a PTI query ahead of the Singapore Grand Prix, Norris acknowledged the sport's massive fan base in India (98 million as per latest Formula 1 figures) and said he would love to race there, having driven the track on a simulator.
"Yeah, I've driven, I used to drive it on the sim, on the game. I've never driven the track in real life there, if it's the same track that you went to. It was a very cool track. So I would love to," said Norris.
Norris has never been to India but one of his best friends happens to be Jehan Daruvala, who raced alongside the McLaren driver in his junior formula days. Daruvala could not progress beyond Formula 2 but he and Norris remain close friends.
"I know I have a lot of fans from India, and I remember having Jehan as my teammate, an Indian driver, for many, many years and one of my best friends. And I've still never been to India, so I would love to go to experience it, first of all, but also to go and race there because I'm sure, and I know, that the fans out there love the sport.
"They love Formula 1 and they love sport in general. And I know cricket and things like that are massive out there. So I think it'll be great for Formula 1, and I certainly look forward to it happening," added Norris.
India will have to roll out a red carpet for Formula 1 with many countries making a beeline to host the race.
There are substantial costs involved with annual hosting fees ranging from ₹300 crore to ₹500 crore. Additionally, the track in Greater Noida is in need of serious renovation which would cost anything between ₹150 crore to ₹200 crore.

briefs.headline: ISL | Time for Chennaiyin FC to ‘put everything together’
briefs.bodyText:
Chennaiyin FC enters the Indian Super League season with renewed optimism.
After crawling to the penultimate position in the previous edition — before which it had hastily put together a squad — CFC has learnt that the first part of the journey is as important as the last.
When Chennaiyin takes the field for its opener against FC Goa in Fatorda on Saturday, it will do so with nearly two months of preparation under its belt.
Proper pre-season
“When the club was in talks with me to continue, the first thing I asked was a proper pre-season,” head coach Clifford Miranda said here on Thursday.
“We have had a seven-week pre-season and we are now in the competition period, so it is eight weeks. The club has provided me with what I wanted — timeframe, resources, facilities, friendlies etc. I am pleased with the signings we made... I am even more pleased with how the players have trained and the attitude they have shown. Now it is time for us to put everything together in the games,” Miranda added.
Another area that needed urgent introspection was goal-scoring.
Huge challenge
While Chennaiyin has drafted promising Brazilian forward Ramon Tanque, it is thin on personnel in that department.
“We have a top striker. If he stays fit, he is going to trouble a lot of defences: he is very explosive. The way we have organised our attacking structure, it is not just about Ramon. There are players around him who can arrive in good moments and score.”
CFC will hope it has plenty left in the ‘Tanque’.

briefs.headline: Better late than never for Shreyas
briefs.deck: It took the skipper his 64th try to reach three-figures for the first time in T20s; he will expect the next won’t be as long in coming
briefs.bodyText:
Shreyas Iyer’s return to the international 20-over set-up has been a mixed bag. Jettisoned into the wilderness for more than two and a half years from December 2023 and therefore missing out on India’s back-to-back World Cup triumphs, the right-hander kept plugging away, first leading Kolkata Knight Riders to the title in 2024 and then taking Punjab Kings to the IPL final the following year. Along the way, Shreyas served notice of not just his exceptional batting skills in the middle-order but also a shrewd, calm and astute brain which, allied with his excellent man-management skills, helped him get the best out of his colleagues, India and international, at both outfits.
It’s debatable if Shreyas had reconciled to more time on the T20I sidelines when Suryakumar Yadav skippered the country to a fabulous title defence at home this February-March. Suryakumar, like Shreyas also from Mumbai, was handpicked to succeed Rohit Sharma in July 2024 as India moved on to a new era in the 20-over format. Having run a fantastic ship at the home 50-over World Cup in October-November 2023 when India scythed unbeaten through the draw, only to be felled by Australia in the final, Rohit found a little bit of consolation and worthwhile silverware for his commitment to aggressive batting and to his wonderful captaincy skills by helping India lift their second T20 World Cup trophy, nearly 17 years after Mahendra Singh Dhoni had done the unthinkable in the inaugural edition in South Africa.
Within hours of that grand conquest of the Proteas in Bridgetown, Rohit followed Virat Kohli into T20I retirement. A day later, Ravindra Jadeja called time on his career too, which meant in one fell swoop, India lost a lot of experience and expertise. The process of rebuilding for the title defence, still 20 months away, began in earnest immediately. Contrary to popular perception that pointed to Rohit’s World Cup deputy, Hardik Pandya, taking over as the leader, the decision-making group of chief selector Ajit Agarkar and new head coach Gautam Gambhir – Rahul Dravid’s extension ended with the World Cup success – plumped for Suryakumar, mainly because question marks continued to hang over the all-rounder’s sustained availability, given his repeated dalliances with injury.
Immediate impact
Suryakumar made an immediate impact as batter and captain, leading India to a 3-0 sweep in Sri Lanka in his first assignment in July 2024. But while India continued to stack up victories and dominate the T20I landscape, the dashing batter’s willow started to grow cold from the beginning of 2025. He went the entire calendar year without a single half-century, an unbeaten 47 against Pakistan in the first of three consecutive showdowns in the Asia Cup in Dubai, his highest score in 19 innings. He was, however, in no danger of losing his place because his middling form wasn’t doing any significant or tangible damage to the team’s fortunes. The unbeaten charge to the Asia Cup crown was another feather in his captaincy cap, and when Suryakumar broke the dry run with scores of 32, 82 not out, 57 not out, 8 and 63 against New Zealand in January to kick off 2026, normal service seemed to have been restored.
His best knock in a year and a quarter came in India’s World Cup opener against United States, at his home ground, the Wankhede Stadium. The foreboding sound of silence was deafening as the unfancied Americans worked their way through the Indian top-order with Shadley van Schalkwyk doing the bulk of the damage. At 77 for six in the 13th over, a seismic upset of monumental proportions loomed until the captain came charging to the rescue. Shepherding the lower-order expertly and choosing the right moments – and bowlers – to attack, Suryakumar remained unconquered on a crucial 84, off just 49 deliveries, to catalyse what in the end became a routine 29-run victory.
Unlike in the Americas in 2024 when India were unstoppable, even on the dicey surfaces in New York, the 2026 run was anything but perfect. India were crushed by South Africa in their first Super Eight encounter in Ahmedabad, which meant that if Suryakumar was to hold the trophy aloft at the same venue two weeks later, his side had to come through four consecutive must-win encounters. India were compelled to rejig their batting order to break up an all-left top three, and Sanju Samson answered the prayers by shedding a lean trot with three blazing knocks on the bounce, culminating in a breathtaking 89 against New Zealand in the title clash.
But while India gathered momentum and peaked at the right time, Suryakumar’s form was patchy. He wasn’t terrible – he did conjure 32 against Pakistan on a dicey Premadasa Stadium surface in Colombo, weighed in with 34 against the Netherlands and delivered the final kick with a 13-ball 33 against Zimbabwe in Chennai – which, coupled with the fact that India became the first nation to successfully defend the World Cup and to win at home, should have earned him a longer rope. At least one more assignment at the very least.
Moving on
But no. Agarkar’s panel decided enough was enough, that it was time to move on post-haste from the Suryakumar era and turn to a fresh face who would be around for the next World Cup, in Australia and New Zealand in October-November 2028. Suryakumar was 35 and a half at the time of the successful defence, which further encouraged the core panel to invest in a younger man. And thus transpired the 31-year-old Shreyas’ return to a format in which he had held his own, but from which he was forcibly excluded because there was no place for him in the crowded middle-order.
The contention was that Shreyas was too good a player to be picked in the 15 and be kept out of the 11, in which the marked emphasis was on multi-skilled players. Like Suryakumar, Shreyas is a batter alone, and the think-tank felt it was difficult to have both right-handers in the mix. But when the call to move on from the older Mumbaikar was made, Shreyas became an automatic choice – as batter and, in the eyes of those occupying the corridors of power, as the captain.
Shreyas must have felt the weight of the world on his shoulders on his comeback. Never mind that he had 150 international appearances across all three formats to his credit, the return to the 20-over iteration was inevitably and understandably accompanied by butterflies and nervous anticipation. His baptism was the stuff nightmares are made of. India were stunned 2-0 by Ireland and then surrendered a five-match series 4-0 in England (the first game was abandoned). Shreyas held his own with the bat – 68, 37, 5, 80 not out and 28 against the English – but he needed to start moving into the black column from the predominantly red one when it came to team victories.
The tide had to turn, because India were too good a team to keep courting defeats. They were caught out by the conditions in the United Kingdom and were slow to react and adapt, but once they travelled to Harare in July for a three-match showdown against Zimbabwe, they have embarked on a stunning course correction that has netted them 10 wins on the bounce, among them Tuesday’s eight-wicket pounding of West Indies in the first of five matches in Lucknow.
India crushed Zimbabwe 3-0, ran rings around Afghanistan in Delhi last month by an identical scoreline, then eked out a narrow two-run win over Japan in Sano just before the start of the Asian Games. It was a five-over fixture on a terribly slow pitch where the ball turned a mile and all 10 overs were sent down by the spinners. India only managed 32 in their five overs – can you even believe that? – and got somewhat lucky in restricting the Japanese to 30, but 12 days later, they defended their Asian Games gold medal with a very good win over Pakistan in the final in Nisshin.
Shreyas thus became the second Indian after Ruturaj Gaikwad to lead the cricket team to the Asiad gold, though he had the luxury of a full-strength side including Jasprit Bumrah, the perennial game-changer. While those nine victories in a row were commendable, Shreyas the batter hadn’t really left a lasting impression. He did have a clutch of 20s – five of them, to be exact – but there wasn’t the defining knock that he would have been desperate for.
That came on Tuesday in Lucknow. Jet-lagged and almost running on empty after having made the long haul from Nisshin to the Uttar Pradesh capital just two days before the contest – the Asian Games final was on October 3, this West Indies fixture was on October 6 – Shreyas put mind over matter in a sterling exhibition of stroke-making, comprehensively eclipsing the multitude of power-hitters under Shai Hope’s command and his own trio of ball-bashers in Abhishek Sharma, Samson and Ishan Kishan.
India’s bowlers had done remarkably well to bowl the visitors out for 171, and while they were not in any great danger even at 35 for two, given the depth in their batting, they needed a partnership to calm slightly jangling nerves. Enter Shreyas, stage left, to reduce it to a no-contest, embarking on a majestic display of controlled, risk-free aggression that left the former two-time World Cup winners scurrying for cover.
Dominant
Completely dominating an unbroken third-wicket stand of 137 with Kishan, Shreyas brought up his first T20I ton off the penultimate ball of the chase, off 42 deliveries. He needed just 14 balls for his second 50, courtesy six towering sixes as the ball went exactly where he intended it to. Abhishek and Kishan and some of the others have made it a fine art of battering the hapless cricket ball. Shreyas chose a less violent methodology, but the impact was still as bruising – perhaps even more so – because there is little that can match the beauty of orthodoxy even in the hustle and bustle of the 20-over version.
It took Shreyas his 64th try to reach three-figures for the first time. Given that the No. 4 slot is entirely his own – he has batted there all 17 times since assuming the captaincy mantle – one can safely surmise that the next won’t be as long in coming.

briefs.headline: APL: Royals begin title defence in style
briefs.deck: Knights rally to edge Marathas; Archers beat Chiefs
briefs.bodyText:
In a repeat of the inaugural season’s final, Rajputana Royals began the defence of its Archery Premier League title in style, beating Prithviraaj Yodhas 5-3 in the opening match of Season 2 at the People’s Plaza on Thursday.
Compound archers Ojas Deotale and Ella Gibson led the way for Royals at the start, with Mete Gazoz giving good support. After a slow start, Abhishek Verma-led Yodhas bounced back and came close to taking the match into a hit-or-miss shoot-off before Mathias Grande shot only an eight with the final arrow.
The second contest of the night saw Mighty Marathas suffer a collapse against Kakatiya Knights. Marathas won the first two sets before losing the next two and then stumbled in the shoot-off.
Nico Wiener and Neeraj Chauhan nailed the inner X-ring in the shoot-out after Marathas, who paid the price for substituting out Dhiraj Bommadevara for the final two sets, let slip a 4-0 advantage.
In the final match of the night, Chero Archers defeated Chola Chiefs 5-3. Archers took the first set but Chiefs fought back to level the match 2-2.
In the final set, Chikitha Taniparthi and Rajat Chauhan couldn’t apply the early pressure on Archers as they dropped a couple of 9s. Archers saw their compounds give them the perfect start. Casey Kaufhold with the penultimate arrow made it tricky but it didn’t matter in the end.
Earlier, India’s Asian Games medallists were felicitated by Vakiti Srihari, Telangana’s Sports Minister, A.P. Jithender Reddy, Telangana Olympic Association president, and APL director Anil Kamineni.
The results: Rajputana Royals bt Prithviraaj Yodhas 5-3 (75-69, 73-74, 77-77, 76-75).
Kakatiya Knights tied with Mighty Marathas 4-4 (73-76, 74-77, 75-66, 77-70). Knights won 2-0 on shoot-off.
Chola Chiefs lost to Chero Archers 3-5 (69-74, 71-70, 75-79, 73-73).
